Listen to this article Share Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala has reportedly suffered a second seizure since revealing that he has a neurological disorder, raising fresh concerns about his health. Advertisement Advertisement The 23-year-old experienced the incident during training on Monday, according to an AFP report on Sunday. Musiala previously collapsed twice on the pitch during pre-season before disclosing that he had a neurological disorder that could cause “temporary but treatable seizures”. Read Also: Musiala reveals neurological disorder after second on-field collapse Monday’s incident was the second since his announcement. The German international is reportedly adjusting his medication to manage the condition while continuing his playing career. The latest development comes amid growing tensions between Bayern and the footballers’ union FIFPRO over the club’s treatment of Musiala and reported pressure on him to renegotiate his contract, which was extended in 2025. Advertisement “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Bayern supervisory board member and former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge on Friday suggested the midfielder could face a pay cut if he fails to rediscover his previous form. Advertisement “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency – because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Related News Political thuggery: Police ineptitude or compromise?
